text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 5th in history:
1249 - In the Sixth Crusade, Louis IX of France landed in Egypt.
1316 - Louis X, King of France from 1314 and known as "The Quarrelsome", died.
1723 - Adam Smith, Scottish political economist and philosopher and author of "The Wealth of Nations", born.
1806 - Holland was declared a kingdom with Louis Bonaparte as its king.
1826 - Carl Maria von Weber, German composer and pianist, died.
1873 - Under pressure from the British, the Sultan of Zanzibar signed a treaty abolishing slavery.
1878 - Francisco Pancho Villa, Mexican guerrilla leader and revolutionary, born.
1883 - John Maynard Keynes, British economist whose theories had worldwide influence, born.
1898 - Federico Garcia Lorca, Spanish poet, playwright and one of the most important figures in modern Spanish literature, born.
1900 - British troops under Redvers Buller captured Pretoria in the Boer War.
1916 - Lord Horatio Herbert Kitchener of Khartoum, Irish soldier, statesman and conqueror of Sudan, was lost at sea when his ship struck a mine off the Orkneys.
1921 - Georges Leon Jules Marie Feydeau, French playwright, actor and director notably of farces, died.
1928 - Tony Richardson, British film and theatre director, born; he won an Oscar for "Tom Jones".
1939 - Joe Clark, youngest-ever Canadian prime minister, born. He held the post for just one year.
1944 - The first British gliders touched down on French soil in preparation for D-Day.
1945 - At the end of World War Two, the Allied Control Commission took control of Germany, dividing it into four occupation zones.
1947 - U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall announced his plan to help Europe recover financially from the effects of World War Two.
1953 - King Frederick signed the new Danish constitution into effect, under which Greenland and the Faroes became integral parts of Denmark.
1954 - Greece, Turkey and Yugoslavia announced they had formed a Balkan Alliance.
1963 - British War Minister John Profumo resigned from government and parliament after admitting he had lied to the House of Commons about his affair with call-girl Christine Keeler.
1967 - The Six-Day War between Israel and her Arab neighbours Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Iraq and Lebanon began.
1968 - U.S. Senator Robert Kennedy was shot in Los Angeles by Palestinian-Arab Sirhan Sirhan. He died the next day.
1975 - The Suez Canal was reopened to all but Israeli shipping after eight years by Egyptian President Anwar Sadat.
1975 - In the first ever referendum in Britain, citizens voted by a 2-1 majority to stay in the Common Market.
1984 - Fuad Mohieddin, Egyptian prime minister since 1982, died of a heart attack.
1988 - Solo yachtswoman Kay Cottee sailed into Sydney Harbour to become the first woman to circle the globe alone.
1989 - Solidarity's defeat of the Communists in Poland's first free elections since World War Two was confirmed.
1991 - The South African parliament voted to repeal the apartheid Group Areas Act and Land Acts of 1913 and 1936.
1993 - Over 20 Pakistani troops serving with the U.N. in Somalia were killed in an ambush.
